output:
Our Winter School on Elliptic Curves and Modular Forms wrapped up on Saturday. We're tired, and very happy.

Held from 5 to 7 November 2026 in Seminar Hall 2, Department of Mathematics, Sahyadri Institute of Science, Pune, the school brought together 41 MSc and early PhD participants from 9 states. We received 112 applications and selected participants based on a statement and one reference, so everyone in the room had earned their seat.

Our speakers were Dr. Nilesh Dharmadhikari (Hyderabad), who covered Mordell-Weil, Dr. Sunanda Iyer (Chennai), who lectured on modular forms, and Dr. Tomasz Wierzbicki, who joined online from Kraków for computations in Sage. Thank you all for making the time.

Our faculty mentor, Prof. Anuradha Venkatesan, guided the project from the first proposal to the last session. We are deeply grateful for her patience and trust.

The school was funded by a Rs 2.4 lakh student initiative grant from the institute, which covered hostel stay and travel for 18 outstation students. Many of them could not have attended without it.

Thank you to Mr. Prakash Salunke from the office, who sorted out the hostel rooms at 11 pm when the bookings got tangled.

Six PhD students volunteered as TAs and ran the problem sessions. Those sessions were the heart of the school, and we plan to keep that format.

Day two brought an unplanned lesson. The power went out for nearly two hours in the afternoon, laptops died, and we moved the problem session to the canteen with two rolling whiteboards. It turned out to be the best session of the three days.

An MSc student from Silchar also spotted an error in a worked example in Dr. Iyer's notes. She corrected it live and thanked him. That is exactly what a school like this should do.

Small schools like this matter a lot for MSc students. At a big conference, asking a question is hard. Here, they asked, and often.

We hope to run a second edition in late 2027, provided we get funding again.

The slides and problem sheets will be uploaded to the Department of Mathematics website in about two weeks. We'll share the link here when it's up.

Thank you to everyone who came, asked, argued, and stayed to the end.

Ketaki Joglekar, Faizan Mirza and [Your Name]
Organisers
